content.thinking:
I'm editing the formula block to add a line after raw_pm GLIDE noting the dial-stop clamp example: raw 1050 clamps to target 978.1, giving a displayed-minus-true delta of 28.1 without sign flip. I want to verify the claim that the clamp only shrinks |delta| and never flips its sign, so I'm checking an edge case where u_true sits near the far stop to confirm the direction holds.

Actually the sign can flip there — if u_true is 990 and the target clamps to 978.1, displayed-minus-true becomes negative, contradicting "never flips it." I also realize wander itself (±21.9 pm) can flip the sign whenever delta is small, like early in lie_tau when the slew hasn't built up much magnitude yet, so the AC's claim that sign matches s at every sampled frame doesn't hold cleanly — I need to account for wander's onset ramp when deciding how to phrase this accurately.

Given this, I think the best approach is to write the AC in terms of slew_pm minus u_true (excluding wander noise), and explicitly document two bounded exceptions: the clamp-edge case where truth sits within W_M of a stop (causing a flip of at most W_M), and the glide-lag case where a truth ramp can cause the delta to overshoot and flip sign as the slew catches up — which matches the D.3 example showing displacement going from +100 to -400.

This is a lag of presentation toward truth, not a departure chosen against direction, so the acceptance criteria should allow a transient sign flip during a step test but otherwise require sign(target_pm - u_true) to equal s at every sampled frame, except when lie_tau is 0 or the truth sits within W_M of the stop on side s.

I'll also require sign(slew_pm - u_true) = s once the slew has converged to within epsilon of the target, keeping this consistent with D.3's slew exception, and note this adjustment where I edit the D.3 formula block.

`s = d x c_dial` for kind GLIDE, with `d = +1` for COMFORT and `-1` for ALARM (the entry's published `direction`), `c_dial = sgn(mid(OK) - mid(A))`, `mid([lo, hi]) = (lo + hi) / 2`, using the calibration record's OK interval and its alarm interval `A` (PF-45); `s` is latched at the lie's first listed frame (and at `hard_start`) and is a function of the entry's `direction` and the static record only. If a record holds more than one alarm interval, `A` is the one whose nearest edge is closest to `u_true` at that frame (MVP dials hold one, so `s` is static); `mid(OK) = mid(A)` is a malformed record (PF-44: honest path, `lie_unrenderable`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `direction`)*

A needle lie therefore always has GLEAM plus a motion mode. It is a weak lie, not an unleaked one, and Sanity's pre-draw gate should refuse a subject with no room (OQ-PF-38).

content.content: 351	*Rule.* A lying digital readout either **ticks continuously** (kind GLIDE: the digit tracks the glide) or **holds stale** (kinds FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL: the digit holds the false target while the ship changes), chosen by hash per lie. The readout is the card numeral (the `displayed_value` of the needle ref's `Perceived`); TICK and STALE govern that numeral only, while the needle draws `displayed_pm` with the never-rest wander in every non-HONEST mode (PF-8; Instruments C2, OQ-IW-19). Honest numerals update on the shared hold grid `HONEST_TICK_MS` (500 ms, HUD-owned; at most one step per grid boundary, then-current value, never queued) and never tween (registry `honest_numeral`; the grid amends art bible 7.3's "one step per real change", ratified 2026-10-27, user ruling X9/D91 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*). The tick interval is `LIE_TICK_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (registered; default 400 ms; range 334 to 1000): the floor is **334 ms**, because a 333 ms interval is 3.003 transitions per second against AC-SN-149 "no more than 3 per second" and the registered intent of `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3. Lying readouts that share a region (a ninth of the displayed picture, counting HUD-layer readouts) share one scheduler: `T_tick = max(LIE_TICK_MS, N_r * 334)` with phases staggered, so the sum of transitions in any rolling second stays at most 3 (D.9); a tick is a digit-glyph substitution, never an inversion of a plate. The inspect card calls the same `perceived(ref)` as its wall gauge, so it lies exactly when the gauge lies, from stage 1 (HR-14, IA-38); the card frame is an anchor and violet appears only on the reading's glass (ART 4.6).
